history.summary: A 5,349sqft strata villa at The Vision, West Coast (D05), at $3.4M — the headline $635 psf and score_1000 of 989 are an artefact of the enormous floor area, not a bargain. As a $3.4M, 5,349sqft leasehold strata villa it is one of the most illiquid product types in Singapore, with a buyer pool measured in handfuls.
history.rating_rationale: The score is a PSF illusion: $635 psf looks cheap only because the 5,349sqft denominator is a strata villa, the rarest and hardest-to-exit residential format. URA's $1,584 median PSF applies to normal apartments, not villas, so the comparison is meaningless. At $3.4M and 99-yr leasehold (~88 yrs left, built 2015), the buyer pool is tiny, appreciation is a pedestrian 3.4%/yr, and exit could take many months to years. Wrong product for a 5-7yr investment hold regardless of the flattering metrics.
red_flags: 5,349sqft strata villa — extremely shallow buyer pool, very slow exit
$635 psf and score_1000 989 are denominator artefacts, not value
URA median PSF not comparable to a villa format

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: A 5,349sqft villa has almost no rental market at a yield that works on $3.4M — tenant demand for this size/format is negligible.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: 3.4%/yr on 61 txn is reliable but unexciting, and strata villas typically lag apartment appreciation due to thin demand. Liquidity, not growth rate, is the disqualifier.
